focus: The G5 layout fix and the measurement that decides whether a start-rate gain is real
noveltyJustification: Four findings are new (G5 blast radius, G5 reproduction gap, Codex trust gap, scorer brief blind spot) and one partially new (the arm keeps growing, now with fresh counts).
keyQuestions: Which hook or pointer surface must each of the six runtimes have before an advisor recommendation is even offered, and which runtimes are unwired in the pre-arm log?
Why does the model start so few offered commands on each runtime (claude 3/12, codex 0/12, pi 0/12, devin 2/11, opencode 3/7, dsh 2/7), and what does the missing COMMAND line prove about the brief?
Which change to the brief contract or hook wiring raises start rate per runtime, and how does it extend rather than duplicate planned phases 005-008?
How must command files be laid out and installed so a fresh external repository exposes every command on every runtime, given the g5 skill.md folder-shadowing result?

label: G5 has a one-namespace blast radius: only create/skill.md exists, its Claude mirror symlink is generated at .claude/commands/create/skill.md, and the shadow hides exactly 12 sibling create commands.
G5 is not proven on the real .claude/commands path: the experiment listed a stand-in skill folder, so a reproduce-first test with a temporary CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR is required before changing layout.

Codex pre-arm runs had no advisor because the arena is untrusted: hooks need per-entry approval stored in ~/.codex/config.toml, no arena project entry exists, and 0 of 6 raw transcripts contain Advisor:.

The scorer cannot attribute a start to the brief: raw Claude transcripts contain Advisor: 6 of 6 while normalized records contain it 0 of 6, Pi is 6 of 6 in-prompt, and OpenCode 1 of 6, so offered-versus-declined is unmeasurable without a hook-recorded brief.

The pre-arm log grew between iterations from 24/24/24/13/10/10 to 24/24/24/15/13/11 rows per runtime, so any summary number is a snapshot and a before/after comparison needs an arm-completeness guard.

reason: Codex never received a brief in the arena because project hooks were unapproved; 0 of 6 raw transcripts contain Advisor:.
